chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Shihab said:

I asked him about a boy of ten years old who performs Hajj. He said: 'Upon him is the Hajj of Islam when he experiences nocturnal emission, and likewise for the girl, Hajj is upon her when she menstruates.'

key_terms.اِبْنُ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ: son of ten years (referring to a ten-year-old boy)
key_terms.اِحْتَلَمَ: experienced nocturnal emission (sign of male puberty)
key_terms.حَجَّةُ اَلْإِسْلاَمِ: the obligatory Hajj (the first one that fulfills the duty)

ai.seo_question: At what age does Hajj become obligatory for children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes ten years as the threshold for Hajj obligation, contingent upon the actual occurrence of puberty signs (nocturnal emission for boys, menstruation for girls) rather than age alone. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that the duty of Hajj is tied to the capacity and maturity indicated by these biological markers, ensuring the pilgrim is fully accountable.
